title_en: United Airlines Pilot Suspended On TSA Orders Over Support For Terror Group, Report Says
title_zh: 报告称，美国联合航空公司飞行员因支持恐怖组织而被运输安全管理局停职
summary: United's reported pilot suspension comes amid growing concerns over insider threats to aviation and renewed scrutiny of airline security.
summary_zh: 据报道，美联航飞行员被停职的原因是人们越来越担心航空业面临的内部威胁以及对航空公司安全的重新审查。
body_en: Paul has had a career of 25+ years focused on the international technology sector, which has taken him to over 100 countries. Along the way, he developed a deep love for aviation, with a travel bucket list measured by aircraft types flown rather than destinations reached. Now he brings that avgeek passion, along with the journalism experience he accumulated early in his career, to write insightful pieces for Simple Flying.

The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) has reportedly directed United Airlines to suspend a pilot last week over alleged support for a terrorist organization. According to a report by Jewish News Syndicate (JNS) , citing a federal government source, the pilot's crew security credential was also revoked. Neither the pilot's identity nor the terrorist organization they allegedly supported has been disclosed.

The reported intervention follows several controversies surrounding United pilots and comes amid heightened international scrutiny of aviation personnel following an attempted terrorist attack aboard a flydubai flight in September. CNN reports that US security agencies have subsequently issued a joint advisory to the aviation industry warning of renewed calls for attacks against commercial aviation.
TSA Reportedly Orders United To Suspend Pilot

The federal intervention reportedly occurred between November 16 and 22, and included the withdrawal of the pilot's Known Crewmember (KCM) credential, which facilitates expedited security screening for eligible airline employees. The existing program is already undergoing significant changes, with the Association of Flight Attendants confirming that its replacement, the Crewmember Access Point (CMAP) program, will be administered directly by the TSA by the end of 2026.

The suspension follows earlier reporting by journalist Mike Wagenheim on November 17, citing two sources who alleged that United was aware of up to six additional crew members who had expressed support for terrorist organizations. According to View From The Wing , the federal source subsequently alleged that resistance from the pilots' union contributed to the TSA's decision to intervene.

JNS approached both United and the TSA for comment on multiple occasions, but was not able to obtain a response from either organization. However, Michael Wilson, spokesperson for United's Master Executive Council of the Air Line Pilots Association (ALPA), explained that the union assesses allegations against its professional ethics code and United's workplace guidelines, stating that
“[The union] has a robust professional standards committee and legal team that evaluates any accusation or pilot action.”
United's Previous Controversies Over Pilot Conduct

The latest case follows renewed scrutiny of United Captain Ibrahim Mossallam, a Newark-based pilot qualified to operate the Boeing 757 and 767. United initially suspended Mossallam with pay in November 2023 after he published social media comments praising the October 7 Hamas-led attacks on Israel. According to Airline Ratings , he subsequently returned to flying duties, although Aerotime reported last month that United had confirmed that he had again been removed from service pending a review.

A separate controversy emerged in October when the Jerusalem Post reported that Israeli authorities had barred United pilot Sina Amjadian from operating flights into the country following allegations of support for Hezbollah and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). However, United responded that Amjadian, a Boeing 737 pilot, was not qualified on United's long-haul aircraft, and had been on leave since 2024.
Mossallam publishes controversial comments concerning the October 7 attacks.
Mossallam reportedly returns to flying duties.
United confirms Mossallam has again been withheld from service.
United denies reports of Mossallam's immediate reinstatement.
Israel's restrictions on Amjadian become public.
Allegations emerge concerning six additional crew members.
TSA reportedly orders the suspension of an unnamed pilot.
Details of the reported TSA intervention are published.

While United has confirmed the employment status of both previously identified pilots, several other allegations remain unverified. The carrier has also explicitly denied reports that Mossallam returned to flying immediately after his latest suspension . Nevertheless, the reported intervention by federal authorities raises important questions about where an airline's responsibility for assessing potential security threats ends, and the government's begins.
body_zh: Paul 拥有超过 25 年的职业生涯，专注于国际技术领域，足迹遍及 100 多个国家。一路走来，他对航空产生了深深的热爱，他的旅行愿望清单是根据飞行的飞机类型而不是到达的目的地来衡量的。现在，他带着这种平均极客的热情，以及他在职业生涯早期积累的新闻经验，为《简单飞行》撰写了富有洞察力的文章。
据报道，美国运输安全管理局（TSA）上周指示联合航空公司暂停一名涉嫌支持恐怖组织的飞行员。据犹太新闻辛迪加（JNS）援引联邦政府消息人士的报道，飞行员的机组安全凭证也被吊销。飞行员的身份和他们据称支持的恐怖组织都没有被披露。
据报道，这次干预行动是在围绕美联航飞行员的几项争议之后进行的，并且在 9 月份迪拜航空航班上发生未遂恐怖袭击事件后，国际社会对航空人员进行了更严格的审查。美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 报道称，美国安全机构随后向航空业发出联合咨询，警告再次呼吁对商业航空发动袭击。
据报道，运输安全管理局命令美联航暂停飞行员
据报道，联邦干预发生在 11 月 16 日至 22 日之间，其中包括吊销飞行员的已知机组成员 (KCM) 证书，该证书有助于对符合条件的航空公司员工进行快速安全检查。现有计划已经发生重大变化，空乘人员协会确认其替代方案——机组成员接入点 (CMAP) 计划将在 2026 年底前由 TSA 直接管理。
此次停职是在记者迈克·瓦根海姆 (Mike Wagenheim) 于 11 月 17 日早些时候报道后，援引两名消息人士的话称，美联航知道另外多达六名机组人员曾表示支持恐怖组织。据 View From The Wing 报道，联邦消息人士随后声称，飞行员工会的抵制促使运输安全管理局决定进行干预。
JNS 多次联系美联航和美国运输安全管理局征求意见，但均未得到任何组织的回应。然而，美联航飞行员协会 (ALPA) 总执行委员会发言人迈克尔·威尔逊 (Michael Wilson) 解释说，工会正在评估针对其职业道德准则和美联航工作场所指南的指控，并表示
“[工会]拥有强大的专业标准委员会和法律团队，可以评估任何指控或试点行动。”
美联航此前就飞行员行为引发的争议

最新案件发生之前，联合航空机长易卜拉欣·莫萨拉姆 (Ibrahim Mossallam) 接受了重新审查。易卜拉欣·莫萨拉姆是一名总部位于纽瓦克的飞行员，有资格驾驶波音 757 和 767 飞机。 联合航空最初于 2023 年 11 月对莫萨拉姆停薪，此前他在社交媒体上发表评论，赞扬 10 月 7 日哈马斯领导的对以色列的袭击。据《航空公司评级》报道，他随后重返飞行岗位，尽管 Aerotime 上个月报道称，美联航已确认他再次被停职等待审查。
10 月，《耶路撒冷邮报》报道称，以色列当局禁止美联航飞行员西娜·阿姆贾迪安 (Sina Amjadian) 运营飞往该国的航班，原因是该机长被指控支持真主党和伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队 (IRGC)，这引发了另一场争议。不过，美联航回应称，波音 737 飞行员 Amjadian 不具备搭乘美联航长途飞机的资格，自 2024 年以来一直处于休假状态。
Mossallam 发表了有关 10 月 7 日袭击事件的有争议的评论。
据报道，莫萨拉姆重返飞行岗位。
美联航确认莫萨拉姆再次停止服务。
曼联否认有关莫萨拉姆立即复职的报道。
以色列对阿姆贾迪安的限制被公开。
又出现了关于另外六名船员的指控。
据报道，运输安全管理局下令暂停一名未透露姓名的飞行员的职务。
所报告的 TSA 干预的详细信息已公布。
虽然美联航已经确认了之前确定的两名飞行员的就业状况，但其他几项指控仍未得到证实。该航空公司还明确否认了有关莫萨拉姆在最近一次停飞后立即恢复飞行的报道。然而，据报道，联邦当局的干预引发了重要问题：航空公司评估潜在安全威胁的责任从何开始，而政府的责任又从何开始。

title_en: The 5 Biggest Airbus A220 Fleets In 2026 Don't Even Include The Jet's Launch Operator
title_zh: 2026 年 5 最大的空客 A220 机队甚至不包括该喷气式飞机的发射运营商
summary: The leading carriers entrusting their regional network to the smallest of Airbus' jets.
summary_zh: 领先的航空公司将其区域网络委托给最小的空客飞机。
body_en: Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

Air France took delivery of its 60th Airbus A220-300 on November 6, closing out a five-year narrowbody renewal program. That milestone underscores the regional jet's growing global fleet and its place among the world's largest operators. Joining the French flag carrier on that podium are two airlines that exclusively fly the A220 : Breeze Airways, with 57 and growing, and airBaltic's 55-strong fleet.

The budget carriers on opposite sides of the Atlantic Ocean join Delta Air Lines, which boasts 92 as of now, and JetBlue Airways with 65, to round out the top five. Notably, SWISS International Air Lines, which was the launch customer for the airframe, still owns just 30 aircraft. The jet's difficult development and launch after Airbus acquired the platform from Bombardier is just one part of the story.

The A220 began as the CSeries before Airbus acquired a controlling stake in 2018. The Swiss order ended after it replaced its aging Avro RJ100 regional fleet, partly due to the ongoing engine crisis that has plagued the plane despite the otherwise popular airframe. Persistent durability issues and supply-chain bottlenecks with the Pratt & Whitney PW1500G engines forced operators worldwide to ground jets and even strip some for viable powerplants, keeping as many flying as possible.

Latvian flag carrier airBaltic introduced the stretched A220-300 in December 2016 and retired every turboprop and Boeing 737 by 2020 to run a pure single-type fleet. The most recent data places the carrier fifth globally with 55 aircraft listed on its roster, according to Airport Spotting. However, not all of those are airworthy. Groundings peaked at 13 parked jets in early 2025 , wiping out thousands of seasonal flights across Europe and forcing costly replacement wet leases.

Restructuring plans shrink the active fleet from 54 jets to 36 by year-end and put 40 undelivered orders under review, even though the airframe itself never caused the crisis. Operated purely on its merits, the airframe exceeded expectations across both scheduled flying and wet lease contracts. Its low fuel burn let airBaltic restart routes profitably at lower passenger loads after the pandemic while leasing up to 13 aircraft to SWISS and Lufthansa Group partners.

Flying one 145-seat cabin simplified crew training, cut maintenance complexity, and supported flights stretching 3,450 nautical miles (6,389 km) from Riga to leisure markets like Tenerife. The vulnerability sat beneath the wing, where the A220 certifies only Pratt & Whitney's PW1500G geared turbofan.

When metal defects in turbine blades triggered urgent inspections and stretched engine overhauls past 200 days, airBaltic had no alternative supplier to fall back on. Engine availability recovered early this year, yet years of grounded aircraft left airBaltic financially fragile when unhedged fuel bills spiked following the recent conflict in Iran. On September 14, the carrier filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New York, naming Pratt as its largest creditor.

Air France secured third place globally on November 6 when its 60th A220-300 arrived in Paris before opening service to Prague three days later, per Airline Geeks. That handover fulfilled the 2019 commitment to retire outdated Airbus A318 and A319 aircraft serving its network. Five years after entering service, the 148-seat fleet has carried nearly 24 million passengers and established the A220-300 as Air France's new medium-haul mainstay.

Finishing the original batch roughly a year behind its initial 2025 target still left four 20-year-old A318s on the winter schedule. Industry-wide delivery delays and Pratt's PW1500G recalls tightened spare availability. As a result, Air France extended A318 operations to March 27, 2027. Rather than stopping at 60 jets, however, Paris now anticipates a 61st A220's arrival and is keeping 30 options plus 30 purchase rights.

Route economics and passenger demand are driving Air France-KLM Group leadership to envision growing toward 90 or 95 A220s. Its five-abreast cabin puts 80% of travelers in a window or aisle seat with 20% more overhead bin volume, while free high-speed WiFi already reaches 85% of the fleet, with full installation expected by February 2027.

JetBlue holds second place globally after counting 66 A220-300s in October out of its 100-aircraft total order, according to the Center for Aviation. That expansion completed the carrier's September 2025 phase-out of the Embraer E190. Trading 100-seat E190s for 140-seat A220-300s cut operating costs per seat by 29% and fuel burn per seat by 40%, projecting $4 million to $5 million in annual gains per jet.

Meanwhile, passengers benefit from bigger seats measuring 18.6 inches (47 centimeters) wide, the roomiest economy seating in JetBlue's fleet. That comes alongside 35 inches (89 centimeters) of pitch in extra-legroom rows and 32 inches (81 centimeters) in standard rows. The jets also have upgraded seatback screens and free high-speed WiFi.

Even at scale, JetBlue saw disruption from Pratt's engine recall as well as the Airbus factory bottlenecks in Mirabel and Mobile. Fiscal reports showed the airline opened the year with four aircraft parked over PW1500G shortages. After engine removal, the planes spent roughly 200 days in overhaul shops. Supply-chain delays also forced Airbus to trim JetBlue's delivery schedule, pushing its final three firm aircraft into 2030 and beyond.

Eliminating the E190 still consolidated JetBlue into an exclusively Airbus operator, streamlining pilot and mechanic qualifications alongside its A320 and A321neo fleets. The transition also unlocked longer transcontinental routes for its smallest aircraft.

Breeze climbed to fourth worldwide when its final Embraer E190 revenue flight landed in New Orleans from Orlando on September 7, following acceptance of the 57th A220 in July , per Airport Spotting. This autumn deliveries pushed the Salt Lake City carrier over 60 jets out of 90 firm orders and 30 options for more. That fleet blueprint follows the design of Chief Executive David Neeleman when he ordered 60 jets in 2018, right after Airbus took over the program.

Neeleman revisited the decision in an Aerospace Global News story in September of this year, saying: "Our long-term strategy has always been to leverage the strengths and efficiencies of the Airbus A220-300 to help us cost-effectively scale our unique business model which centers around offering affordable, nonstop flights from unserved and underserved markets."
body_zh: 卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
法航于 11 月 6 日接收了第 60 架空客 A220-300，结束了为期五年的窄体机更新计划。这一里程碑凸显了支线喷气式飞机全球机队规模的不断扩大及其在全球最大运营商中的地位。与法国国旗航空公司一起登上领奖台的还有两家专门运营 A220 飞机的航空公司：微风航空 (Breeze Airways)，拥有 57 架且还在不断增加；波罗的海航空 (airBaltic) 拥有 55 架机队。
大西洋两岸的廉价航空公司与达美航空（目前拥有 92 架飞机）和捷蓝航空（65 架）一起跻身前五名。值得注意的是，作为该机身的启动客户的瑞士国际航空公司仍然只拥有 30 架飞机。空中客车公司从庞巴迪手中收购该平台后，这款喷气式飞机的艰难开发和推出只是故事的一部分。
A220 最初是空客在 2018 年收购控股权之前的 C 系列。瑞士的订单在替换了老化的 Avro RJ100 支线机队后终止，部分原因是尽管机身很受欢迎，但持续的发动机危机一直困扰着该飞机。普惠 PW1500G 发动机持续存在的耐用性问题和供应链瓶颈迫使世界各地的运营商将喷气式飞机停飞，甚至拆除一些飞机以换取可行的动力装置，以保持尽可能多的飞行。

拉脱维亚旗舰航空公司波罗的海航空于 2016 年 12 月推出了加长型 A220-300，并于 2020 年退役了所有涡轮螺旋桨飞机和波音 737，以运营纯单一机型机队。根据 Airport Spotting 的最新数据，该航空公司拥有 55 架飞机，在全球排名第五。然而，并非所有这些都适合航空。 2025 年初，停飞飞机数量达到顶峰，有 13 架飞机停飞，导致欧洲各地数千架季节性航班停飞，并迫使人们进行成本高昂的更换湿租。
重组计划到年底将现役飞机从 54 架减少到 36 架，并对 40 架未交付的订单进行审查，尽管机身本身并未引发危机。纯粹凭借其优点，该机身超出了定期飞行和湿租合同的预期。波罗的海航空的低油耗让波罗的海航空在疫情结束后以较低的载客量重新启动航线并实现盈利，同时向瑞航和汉莎航空集团合作伙伴租赁了多达 13 架飞机。
驾驶一间 145 座的客舱简化了机组人员培训，降低了维护复杂性，并支持从里加飞往特内里费岛等休闲市场 3,450 海里（6,389 公里）的航班。该漏洞位于机翼下方，A220 仅认证普惠公司的 PW1500G 齿轮传动涡轮风扇发动机。
当涡轮叶片的金属缺陷引发紧急检查并延长发动机大修时间超过 200 天时，波罗的海航空没有其他供应商可以依靠。发动机可用性于今年年初恢复，但由于最近伊朗冲突导致未对冲的燃油费用飙升，多年来飞机停飞导致波罗的海航空财务状况脆弱。 9月14日，该航空公司在纽约根据美国破产法第11章申请破产保护，普拉特为其最大债权人。
据 Airline Geeks 报道，法航于 11 月 6 日获得全球第三名，其第 60 架 A220-300 飞机抵达巴黎，三天后开通飞往布拉格的航班。这次移交履行了 2019 年退役过时空客 A318 和 A319 飞机的承诺。投入运营五年后，拥有 148 个座位的机队已运送了近 2400 万名乘客，使 A220-300 成为法航新的中程中流砥柱。
最初批次的完成比最初的 2025 年目标晚了大约一年，但冬季计划中仍有四架机龄 20 年的 A318。全行业范围内的交付延迟和普拉特 PW1500G 召回导致备件供应紧张。因此，法航将 A318 的运营期限延长至 2027 年 3 月 27 日。然而，巴黎航空目前预计有 61 架 A220 抵达，并保留 30 架选择权和 30 架购买权，而不是停留在 60 架飞机。
航线经济性和乘客需求正在推动法航荷航集团领导层设想将 A220 飞机数量增加到 90 架或 95 架。其五排并排的客舱可让 80% 的旅客坐在靠窗或靠过道的座位上，头顶行李舱容量增加了 20%，而免费高速 WiFi 已覆盖机队 85% 的用户，预计将于 2027 年 2 月全面安装。
根据航空中心的数据，捷蓝航空 10 月份共订购了 100 架飞机，共订购了 66 架 A220-300，位居全球第二。此次扩建完成了该航空公司于 2025 年 9 月淘汰巴西航空工业公司 E190 的计划。将 100 座 E190 换成 140 座 A220-300 可使每个座位的运营成本降低 29%，每个座位的燃油消耗降低 40%，预计每架飞机的年收益为 400 万至 500 万美元。
与此同时，乘客可以享受宽达 18.6 英寸（47 厘米）的更大座椅，这是捷蓝航空机队中最宽敞的经济舱座椅。与此同时，额外腿部空间行的间距为 35 英寸（89 厘米），标准行的间距为 32 英寸（81 厘米）。喷气式飞机还配备了升级的座椅靠背屏幕和免费高速 WiFi。
即使在规模上，捷蓝航空也看到了普拉特发动机召回以及空客米拉贝尔和莫比尔工厂瓶颈造成的干扰。财务报告显示，该航空公司年初有四架飞机因 PW1500G 短缺而停飞。拆除发动机后，这些飞机在大修车间待了大约 200 天。供应链延误还迫使空中客车公司削减捷蓝航空的交付时间表，将其最后三架飞机的交付时间推迟到 2030 年及以后。
取消 E190 仍然使捷蓝航空成为一家专门的空客运营商，并简化了其 A320 和 A321neo 机队的飞行员和机械师资格。此次转型还为其最小的飞机开启了更长的跨大陆航线。

据 Airport Spotting 报道，继 7 月份接收第 57 架 A220 飞机后，Breeze 的最后一架巴西航空工业公司 E190 营收航班于 9 月 7 日从奥兰多降落在新奥尔良，其排名攀升至全球第四。今年秋季，这家盐湖城航空公司的 90 架确认订单中的 60 多架喷气式飞机的交付量，以及 30 架更多的选择。该机队蓝图遵循首席执行官戴维·尼尔曼 (David Neeleman) 的设计，当时他在 2018 年空中客车接手该项目后订购了 60 架飞机。
尼尔曼在今年 9 月的《航空航天全球新闻》报道中重新审视了这一决定，他表示：“我们的长期战略始终是利用空客 A220-300 的优势和效率，帮助我们经济高效地扩展我们独特的商业模式，该模式的核心是从无服务和服务不足的市场提供价格实惠的直达航班。”

title_en: Qantas Launches 5 New Nonstop Routes For 2027: See Full List Now
title_zh: 澳洲航空 2027 年推出 5 条新直飞航线：立即查看完整列表
summary: Two long-haul and three domestic links will take off next year.
summary_zh: 两条长途航线和三条国内航线将于明年开通。
body_en: James lives and breathes route development. Educated in Air Transport Management at Loughborough University and Cranfield University, James has a PhD in Airline Strategy and Economics. James was Market Opportunity Analyst at London Luton Airport and Chief Analyst at anna.aero. He taught airline strategy and economics to undergraduate and postgraduate students for five years and has worked closely with multiple carriers on route and market intelligence projects. He is based near London, UK.

Qantas is currently set to launch five new routes between January and October 2027 . They include a new link announced on November 26, when this article was written, which will be operated by QantasLink. Of course, compared to some of the other entries, it might not seem particularly noteworthy, but it is in its own right.

As the article only focuses on 2027, the upcoming link from Sydney to Las Vegas, which will begin on December 29, is not included. Qantas will serve this market six times weekly using the Boeing 787-9 . It'll be the first time that scheduled flights have existed, although charter services operated in the past.
Qantas' Five Upcoming Routes In 2027 (For Now)

Obviously, a lot of the attention is on the much-discussed nonstop service from Sydney to London Heathrow , which will deploy the Airbus A350-1000ULR . The maximum block time is expected to be around 21 hours.

Reflecting the highly prestigious nature of the route, AeroRoutes shows that it'll use QF1/QF2, which is currently on Qantas' one-stop operation from Sydney to Heathrow via Singapore. The stopping service will then use QF5/QF6. Those numbers are currently on Sydney-Perth-Rome, which will become QF105/QF106.
3 weekly QantasLink Dash 8-Q400 (Sunstate). See the next section
4 weekly QantasLink E190 (Alliance). Jetstar also operates
3 weekly 787-9. Qantas will now have 3 routes to South Africa. It'll be Cape Town's longest nonstop service in the Southern Hemisphere
The so-called Project Sunrise, and everything related to it, has been discussed in detail on many occasions . Tickets are meant to go on sale in February

Theoretically, the nonstop operation to Heathrow will cover 9,100+ nautical miles (16,853+ km) each way. However, this is before adjusting the distance because of detours for closed airspace and chasing tailwinds and lower airspace costs. It'll cover more distance than that. Still, even before the alteration, it'd exceed the length of what is currently number one, Singapore Airlines to New York JFK, by around 11%.

Questions might be raised about the appeal of the upcoming nonstop service from Albury to the popular Gold Coast, which will have a maximum block time of two hours and 20 minutes on the Q400 . However, QantasLink will be the third airline to attempt it since 2017.

Cirium Diio data shows that the now-defunct JetGo flew in 2017/2018 using the Embraer ERJ135 and ERJ140. The now-defunct carrier Bonza followed in 2023/2024 using the Boeing 737 MAX 8. Bonza primarily focused on unserved markets, whether without head-to-head competition or brand-new.

Like low-cost carriers elsewhere, Bonza used its higher-capacity equipment with much lower seat-mile costs to offer much more attractive fares, compounded by flying nonstop rather than connecting on the way. The lower fares were entirely to drive demand and therefore to grow the market's traffic.

Booking data shows that Albury-Gold Coast passengers increased by nearly 400% to over 23,000 in a year after the airline's entry. Of course, demand stimulation from the lower fares depressed the yields, but that always happens with LCCs. It is unclear if Bonza's fares fell by more or less than the traffic growth. It is unknown what the average fare was to achieve an approximate 80% load factor.

QantasLink's operation will be radically different. It'll deploy the 76-seat Q400 rather than the 189-seat MAX 8, reducing round-trip weekly seats for sale from 1,134 to just 456. It'll not have to discount anywhere near as dramatically. That's just as well, as its much higher costs wouldn't let it, at least not sustainably. That's why its minimum round-trip fare is about USD$344 (AU$518). By only flying at more popular times of the year, rather than for weeks at a time and having to discount more, yields will not be depressed.

QantasLink's new route to the Gold Coast will cover 579 nautical miles (1,072 km) each way. However, if statute miles are used instead, it'll be 666 miles, the so-called number of the beast. Schedule analysis suggests that only 11 routes globally will have this great circle distance when the Q400 service lifts off in March.

It will be Albury's second-longest turboprop-driven scheduled link in nearly three years. QantasLink had operated the Q400 to Brisbane between July 2021 and May 2024, but that route has switched to the 96-seat E190 (other capacities operate occasionally). More seats contributed to the route's frequency falling to daily, down from the record high of two daily flights with the Q400.
body_zh: 詹姆斯与路线开发息息相关。詹姆斯曾就读于拉夫堡大学和克兰菲尔德大学航空运输管理专业，拥有航空公司战略和经济学博士学位。 James 曾任伦敦卢顿机场市场机会分析师和 anna.aero 首席分析师。他向本科生和研究生教授航空公司战略和经济学五年，并与多家航空公司在航线和市场情报项目上密切合作。他居住在英国伦敦附近。
澳洲航空目前计划于 2027 年 1 月至 10 月期间开通 5 条新航线。其中包括 11 月 26 日（撰写本文时）宣布的新链接，该链接将由 QantasLink 运营。当然，与其他一些条目相比，它可能看起来不是特别值得注意，但它本身就是如此。
由于本文仅关注 2027 年，因此未包括即将于 12 月 29 日开通的从悉尼到拉斯维加斯的航线。澳洲航空将使用波音 787-9 每周六次为该市场提供服务。尽管过去曾运营过包机服务，但这将是首次存在定期航班。
澳洲航空 2027 年即将开通的 5 条航线（目前）
显然，人们的注意力集中在备受讨论的从悉尼到伦敦希思罗机场的直达航班上，该航班将使用空客 A350-1000ULR。预计最长出块时间约为 21 小时。
AeroRoutes 表示，该航线将使用 QF1/QF2，这反映了该航线的高度声誉，该航线目前是澳洲航空从悉尼经新加坡飞往希思罗的一站式航线。停止服务将使用 QF5/QF6。这些号码目前位于悉尼-珀斯-罗马，将成为 QF105/QF106。
每周 3 次 QantasLink Dash 8-Q400 (Sunstate)。请参阅下一节
每周 4 班 QantasLink E190（联盟）。捷星航空还运营
3 周 787-9。澳洲航空现将开通 3 条飞往南非的航线。这将是开普敦在南半球最长的直达航班
所谓的日出计划，以及与之相关的一切，已经被多次详细讨论过。门票预计于二月发售
理论上，飞往希思罗机场的直达航班单程航程将超过 9,100 海里（16,853+ 公里）。然而，这是在调整距离之前，因为绕行封闭空域并追逐顺风和降低空域成本。它将覆盖比这更远的距离。尽管如此，即使在改动之前，它的长度也比目前排名第一的新加坡航空飞往纽约肯尼迪机场的航线长了约 11%。
人们可能会对即将开通的从奥尔伯里到热门黄金海岸的直达服务的吸引力提出疑问，该服务在 Q400 上的最长阻塞时间为 2 小时 20 分钟。然而，QantasLink 将成为自 2017 年以来第三家尝试这一举措的航空公司。
Cirium Diio 数据显示，现已停业的 JetGo 在 2017/2018 年使用巴西航空工业公司 ERJ135 和 ERJ140 进行飞行。现已解散的航空公司 Bonza 于 2023/2024 年使用波音 737 MAX 8 紧随其后。Bonza 主要专注于未服务的市场，无论是没有正面竞争的市场还是全新的市场。
与其他地方的低成本航空公司一样，Bonza 利用其容量更大的设备和低得多的座英里成本来提供更具吸引力的票价，再加上直飞航班而不是中途转机，这一点更加复杂。较低的票价完全是为了推动需求，从而增加市场的客流量。
预订数据显示，该航空公司进入后一年内，奥尔伯里-黄金海岸的乘客数量增加了近 400%，达到 23,000 多人。当然，较低票价带来的需求刺激会压低收益率，但低成本航空公司总是会发生这种情况。目前还不清楚 Bonza 的票价下降幅度是否大于或小于客流量的增长幅度。目前尚不清楚要达到大约 80% 的载客率所需的平均票价是多少。
QantasLink 的运营方式将截然不同。它将部署 76 座的 Q400，而不是 189 座的 MAX 8，将每周出售的往返座位从 1,134 个减少到仅 456 个。它不必大幅打折。这也好，因为其更高的成本不允许这样做，至少不可持续。这就是为什么其最低往返票价约为 344 美元（518 澳元）。通过仅在一年中更受欢迎的时间飞行，而不是一次飞行数周并不得不提供更多折扣，收益率不会受到压低。
QantasLink 飞往黄金海岸的新航线单程里程为 579 海里（1,072 公里）。然而，如果用法定英里来代替，那就是666英里，即所谓的野兽之数。时刻表分析表明，当 Q400 航班于 3 月份起飞时，全球只有 11 条航线具有如此大的圆程距离。
这将是奥尔伯里近三年来第二长的涡轮螺旋桨驱动定期航线。 QantasLink 曾于 2021 年 7 月至 2024 年 5 月期间运营 Q400 飞往布里斯班，但该航线已改用 96 座的 E190（其他运力偶尔运营）。座位数增加导致该航线的班次从 Q400 每日两班的历史最高水平降至每日一班。

title_en: US Navy orders three more E-130J Phoenix II nuclear communications aircraft
title_zh: 美国海军再订购三架E-130J凤凰II核通讯机
summary: The US Navy has exercised a $1.13 billion contract option with Northrop Grumman for three more E-130J Phoenix… The post US Navy orders three more E-130J Phoenix II nuclear communications aircraft appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: 美国海军已与诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司行使价值 11.3 亿美元的合同选择权，购买另外三架 E-130J“凤凰”……之后美国海军又订购了三架 E-13
body_en: The US Navy has exercised a $1.13 billion contract option with Northrop Grumman for three more E-130J Phoenix II test aircraft, bringing the number of aircraft under contract for the development of its future airborne nuclear communications platform to six.

According to the Pentagon’s contract announcement for November 25, 2026 , the award covers the design, development and delivery of three system demonstration test aircraft, as well as an initial supply of spare parts. Work is expected to be completed by January 2030.

The US Navy has committed $4.18 million in fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation funds at the time of the award. Most of the work will take place in Melbourne, Florida (35%), Marietta, Georgia (23%), and Richardson, Texas (15%).

The E-130J is based on the stretched C-130J-30 Super Hercules, fitted with Take Charge and Move Out (TACAMO) mission equipment, including a very low frequency (VLF) communications system from Collins Aerospace. Northrop Grumman leads the program, with Collins Aerospace and Lockheed Martin as subcontractors.

The US Navy’s initial $3.46 billion development contract , awarded in December 2024, covered three engineering development aircraft and included options for three additional test aircraft and up to six aircraft in an initial production batch.

The latest award exercises the options for the three additional test aircraft. In March 2026, the US Navy also awarded Northrop Grumman a $225.1 million contract modification for the E-130J’s training systems.

On October 15, 2026, Lockheed Martin delivered the first C-130J-30 airframe for the program to the US Navy at its Marietta facility. The aircraft is due to be handed over to Northrop Grumman for conversion.
E-130J faces mission equipment integration challenges
Fitting the nuclear communications equipment aboard the Super Hercules has proved more challenging than anticipated.

In its Weapon Systems Annual Assessment , published on July 2, 2026, the US Government Accountability Office (GAO) revealed that the program had pushed back its low-rate production decision by about a year.
The watchdog said that integration risks identified in an independent assessment in September 2024 “have morphed into realities.”

Contractors are now working to reduce the weight of existing mission systems so that they can be accommodated aboard the C-130J-30. The program office maintained that the E-130J was on track but, according to the GAO, provided no documentation to support that claim. The aircraft’s planned entry into operational service remains classified.

The E-130J will take over the TACAMO mission currently performed by the US Navy’s 16 Boeing E-6B Mercury aircraft. Its role is to ensure that US national leadership can maintain communications with the country’s nuclear-armed ballistic missile submarines, even in the event of a nuclear conflict. The US Navy named the aircraft Phoenix II in August 2025 .
The post US Navy orders three more E-130J Phoenix II nuclear communications aircraft appeared first on AeroTime .
body_zh: 美国海军已与诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司签订了价值 11.3 亿美元的合同选择权，购买另外三架 E-130J Phoenix II 测试机，从而使用于开发未来机载核通信平台的合同飞机数量达到六架。
根据五角大楼2026年11月25日的合同公告，该合同涵盖三架系统演示测试飞机的设计、开发和交付，以及零配件的初步供应。工程预计将于 2030 年 1 月完成。
授标时，美国海军已承诺在 2027 财年的研究、开发、测试和评估资金中投入 418 万美元。大部分工作将在佛罗里达州墨尔本（35%）、佐治亚州玛丽埃塔（23%）和德克萨斯州理查森（15%）进行。
E-130J 基于加长的 C-130J-30 超级大力神，配备了接管和撤出 (TACAMO) 任务设备，包括柯林斯航空航天公司的甚低频 (VLF) 通信系统。诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司领导该项目，柯林斯航空航天公司和洛克希德·马丁公司作为分包商。
美国海军最初的 34.6 亿美元开发合同于 2024 年 12 月授予，涵盖三架工程开发飞机，并包括另外三架测试飞机和初始生产批次中最多六架飞机的选项。
最新授予的合同行使了另外三架测试飞机的选择权。 2026年3月，美国海军还授予诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司价值2.251亿美元的E-130J训练系统改装合同。
2026 年 10 月 15 日，洛克希德·马丁公司在其玛丽埃塔工厂向美国海军交付了该项目的第一架 C-130J-30 机身。该飞机将移交给诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司进行改装。
E-130J面临任务设备集成挑战
事实证明，在超级大力神号上安装核通信设备比预期更具挑战性。
美国政府问责办公室 (GAO) 在 2026 年 7 月 2 日发布的《武器系统年度评估》中透露，该计划已将其低速生产决定推迟了大约一年。
该监管机构表示，2024 年 9 月的独立评估中发现的整合风险“已变成现实”。
承包商现在正在努力减轻现有任务系统的重量，以便它们可以安装在 C-130J-30 上。项目办公室坚称 E-130J 已步入正轨，但根据 GAO 的说法，没有提供任何文件来支持这一说法。该飞机投入运营的计划仍处于保密状态。
E-130J 将接替目前由美国海军 16 架波音 E-6B Mercury 飞机执行的 TACAMO 任务。它的作用是确保美国国家领导层即使在发生核冲突时也能与该国的核弹道导弹潜艇保持通信。美国海军于2025年8月将这架飞机命名为“凤凰二号”。
美国海军又订购了三架 E-130J Phoenix II 核通信机，这首先出现在 AeroTime 上。

title_en: Why Airline Joint Ventures Are Accused Of Keeping Transatlantic Fares High
title_zh: 为什么航空公司合资企业被指责保持跨大西洋航线的高票价
summary: Alliances make it hard for travelers to find real value in transatlantic prices.
summary_zh: 联盟使旅行者很难在跨大西洋价格中找到真正的价值。
body_en: Jack comes to Simple Flying with a lifelong interest in all things aviation. He holds a degree in Aerospace Engineering from Georgia Tech, and is a certified private and remote pilot. Beyond these experiences, Jack previously worked for a corporate flight department where he gained first-hand experience in the world of business aviation. Currently, Jack works in the professional services industry and continues to build his flight hours outside of work.

Three antitrust-immunized joint ventures now dominate transatlantic aviation: United Airlines with Lufthansa and its Star Alliance partners, Delta Air Lines with Air France-KLM and Virgin Atlantic, and American Airlines with British Airways and Iberia. A Wendover Productions video , as summarized by Pulse , says they control roughly 75% of New York to Europe flights and labels them cartels, a framing that belongs to the video rather than to regulators.

The underlying accusation is more precise: partners who share revenue and set fares together stop competing on the nonstop routes where their networks overlap. Defenders say the same coordination lowers prices for most travelers who connect. Both claims have empirical support, and evidence from the Department of Justice and a study commissioned by the Department of Transportation shows where each holds, where it weakens, and why the argument has persisted for years.

An alliance alone does not permit pricing coordination, since carriers in an arm’s-length codeshare each set their own prices, with the operating airline keeping the revenue and the marketing partner collecting a booking fee. Antitrust immunity changes that arrangement by allowing partners to decide fares, schedules, and other competitively sensitive matters jointly across the routes included in their agreement.

The joint ventures go further by pooling revenue, as partners in a metal-neutral structure share ticket revenue on covered routes under a capacity-based formula, leaving them indifferent about which airline flies a given passenger. A study for the Department of Transportation described the result as carriers behaving like a single airline on the routes in question. American, British Airways, and Iberia argued in 2009 that this removes the incentive to keep a partner’s nonstop flight out of the other carrier’s reach, because a customer choosing it would otherwise transfer revenue away from the selling carrier.

Joint ventures exist partly because ownership rules in the United States and European Union preclude cross-border mergers, making revenue-sharing agreements the closest available substitute for a single airline. DOT approves them under a public interest standard that can weigh foreign policy goals. The video adds that the pooled partners publish matching prices on overlapping flights, citing United and Brussels Airlines selling the same 6:00 PM Brussels departure at the same fare, which it presents as evidence of price fixing.
What Justice Department Economists Found On Nonstop Routes

In a 2011 discussion paper , Antitrust Division economists William Gillespie and Oliver Richard analyzed fares from 2005 to 2010 on 115 routes linking the 20 largest cities in the United States and the European Union. They counted immunized partners serving the same route as a single competitor and found that average one-way fares were $31 higher on routes with one independent nonstop competitor than on routes with two, $62 higher than with three, and $88 higher than with four.

Those gaps equal roughly 7% of the average fare for each competitor lost, and each was statistically significant at the 99% confidence level. The authors read the result as consistent with the ordinary antitrust presumption that reducing competition raises prices, and they observed that nonstop fares averaged 8.3% above connecting fares, yet most economy passengers on the sampled routes still chose nonstop service.

The paper also documents how concentrated the market has become, since three immunized groups, one in each alliance, carried more than 82% of US-EU passenger traffic in the year ending June 2009, and by late 2010 more than half of the sampled routes had a single independent nonstop competitor. Because foreign-carrier fares for itineraries without a US carrier are not public, the economists treated US-carrier fares as representative, a limitation that qualifies any reading of the data. The authors stressed that the paper reflects their own views rather than an official Justice Department position.

Defenders of the structure rely on double marginalization, the idea that when two unaffiliated carriers price their own legs of a connecting trip, each ignores how its markup reduces demand for the other, so the combined fare ends up too high. Partners that share revenue internalize that effect, which should lower fares for itineraries that require both carriers.

A study by economists Jan Brueckner and Ethan Singer , performed under contract to the Department of Transportation and released in 2019, tested the idea on fares from 1997 to 2016. It found that joint venture itineraries were priced about 7.2% below interline tickets, and that their fares were statistically indistinguishable from those of single-carrier trips. On transatlantic routes, the joint venture discount reached roughly 9% across cabins.

The Justice Department paper offered a rebuttal rather than a denial, since its economists agreed that alliances reduce connecting fares relative to interline tickets yet found that within SkyTeam and Star Alliance, immunized itineraries were no cheaper than non-immunized alliance itineraries, implying the pricing benefit does not require immunity. In the 2019 study, alliance partners without immunity priced just 0.7% below interline tickets, compared with 6.4% for immunized partners, which supports the claim that immunity matters. The two bodies of work therefore agree that connecting fares fall under alliances and disagree mainly on whether immunity is what makes them fall. The Justice Department economists added that 68% of US-EU passengers connected in 2009 across all itineraries, which is why the efficiency claim matters even though nonstop routes carry the higher fares.

The same Transportation Department study also found evidence that critics cite, reporting that in the later years of its 1997-2016 sample, granting immunity or joint venture status to two previously unaligned carriers on an overlapping route was equivalent to removing a competitor, with fares rising accordingly. The effect appeared in economy class, where an additional immunized or joint venture pair raised fares by about four to 13% depending on the specification, while business class fares showed no such overlap effect. That finding is notable because most earlier studies had found no nonstop effect, a point the authors flag as unusual.
body_zh: Jack 带着对航空一切事物的终生兴趣加入了 Simple Flying。他拥有佐治亚理工学院的航空航天工程学位，并且是一名经过认证的私人和远程飞行员。除了这些经验之外，杰克还曾在公司飞行部门工作过，在那里他获得了公务航空领域的第一手经验。目前，杰克在专业服务行业工作，并在工作之外继续增加飞行时间。
三个不受反垄断豁免的合资企业目前主导着跨大西洋航空业：联合航空与汉莎航空及其星空联盟合作伙伴、达美航空与法航-荷航和维珍航空、美国航空与英国航空和西班牙国家航空。正如 Pulse 所总结的，Wendover Productions 的一段视频称，他们控制着大约 75% 的纽约飞往欧洲的航班，并将这些航班贴上了卡特尔的标签，这一框架属于视频而非监管机构。
潜在的指控更为准确：共享收入并共同制定票价的合作伙伴停止在其网络重叠的直达航线上进行竞争。捍卫者表示，同样的协调降低了大多数转机旅客的价格。这两种说法都有实证支持，司法部和交通部委托进行的一项研究提供的证据表明了每种说法的正确性、弱点以及为什么这种争论多年来一直存在。
仅靠联盟是不允许进行定价协调的，因为具有一定距离的代码共享的航空公司各自设定自己的价格，运营航空公司保留收入，营销合作伙伴收取预订费。反垄断豁免权改变了这种安排，允许合作伙伴共同决定协议中包含的航线的票价、时刻表和其他竞争敏感事项。

这些合资企业更进一步，通过集中收入，金属中立结构中的合作伙伴根据基于运力的公式分享所覆盖航线的机票收入，从而使他们对哪家航空公司为特定乘客提供飞行服务无关紧要。美国运输部的一项研究将这一结果描述为航空公司在相关航线上的行为就像一家航空公司。美国航空、英国航空和伊比利亚航空在 2009 年辩称，这消除了将合作伙伴的直达航班排除在其他航空公司的覆盖范围之外的动机，因为选择该航班的客户否则会将收入从销售航空公司转移出去。
合资企业存在的部分原因是美国和欧盟的所有权规则禁止跨境合并，这使得收入分享协议成为单一航空公司最接近的替代品。交通部根据可以权衡外交政策目标的公共利益标准批准它们。该视频补充说，联合合作伙伴发布了重叠航班的匹配价格，并援引美联航和布鲁塞尔航空公司的话说，他们以相同的票价出售下午 6:00 布鲁塞尔出发的航班，以此作为价格操纵的证据。
司法部经济学家在直达航线上发现了什么

在 2011 年的一篇讨论文件中，反垄断部门经济学家 William Gillespie 和 Oliver Richard 分析了 2005 年至 2010 年连接美国 20 个最大城市和欧盟的 115 条航线的票价。他们对与单一参赛者提供相同路线的免疫合作伙伴进行了统计，结果发现，有一名独立直达参赛者的路线上的平均单程票价比有两名参赛者的路线高出 31 美元，比有三名参赛者的路线高出 62 美元，比有四名参赛者的路线高出 88 美元。
这些差距大约相当于每个输掉的参赛者平均票价的 7%，并且在 99% 的置信水平下，每个差距都具有统计显着性。作者认为这一结果与减少竞争会提高价格的一般反垄断假设一致，他们观察到直达票价平均比转接票价高出 8.3%，但抽样航线上的大多数经济舱乘客仍然选择直达服务。

该论文还记录了市​​场的集中度，因为在截至 2009 年 6 月的一年中，三个免疫团体（每个联盟各一个）承载了超过 82% 的美国-欧盟客运量，并且到 2010 年底，超过一半的抽样航线都有一个独立的直达竞争对手。由于没有美国航空公司的外国航空公司的行程票价并不公开，经济学家将美国航空公司的票价视为具有代表性的，这是对数据进行任何解读的限制。作者强调，该论文反映了他们自己的观点，而不是司法部的官方立场。
该结构的捍卫者依赖于双重边际化，即当两家独立的航空公司为自己的转机行程定价时，每一方都忽略了其加价如何减少对方的需求，因此最终的总票价过高。分享收入的合作伙伴会将这种影响内部化，这应该会降低需要两家航空公司的行程的票价。
经济学家 Jan Brueckner 和 Ethan Singer 根据交通部合同进行了一项研究，并于 2019 年发布，该研究对 1997 年至 2016 年的票价测试了这一想法。研究发现，合资行程的价格比联运机票低约 7.2%，而且其票价在统计上与单一承运商行程的票价没有区别。在跨大西洋航线上，合资企业的跨舱折扣达到约 9%。

司法部的文件提出了反驳而不是否认，因为其经济学家同意联盟会降低相对于联运机票的转接票价，但发现在天合联盟和星空联盟内部，免疫行程并不比非免疫联盟行程便宜，这意味着定价优势不需要豁免。在 2019 年的研究中，没有免疫力的联盟合作伙伴的票价仅比联运机票低 0.7%，而免疫合作伙伴的价格为 6.4%，这支持了免疫力很重要的说法。因此，两个工作机构一致认为转接票价属于联盟范围，但主要在豁免是否是导致转接票价下降的原因上存在分歧。司法部经济学家补充说，2009 年，68% 的美国-欧盟乘客在所有行程中都进行了转机，这就是为什么尽管直达航线的票价较高，但效率主张很重要。

运输部的同一项研究还发现了批评者引用的证据，报告称，在 1997 年至 2016 年样本的后期，向重叠航线上的两家先前未结盟的航空公司授予豁免权或合资企业地位，相当于消除竞争对手，票价也会相应上涨。这种效应出现在经济舱中，根据规格，额外的免疫舱或合资舱票价提高了约 4% 至 13%，而商务舱票价则没有表现出这种重叠效应。这一发现值得注意，因为大多数早期研究都没有发现不间断的效果，作者认为这一点不寻常。

title_en: Why 97% Of Boeing 777 Pilots Continue An Unstable Approach Instead Of Going Around
title_zh: 为什么 97% 的波音 777 飞行员继续不稳定进场而不是复飞
summary: While most landings follow a stable approach, almost all unstable approaches are followed by landing.
summary_zh: 虽然大多数着陆遵循稳定进近，但几乎所有不稳定进近都是在着陆后进行的。
body_en: Based in the UK, Josh is a keen writer with a degree in Military History. Having worked previously as a financial journalist, he has covered the aviation industry extensively, reporting on airlines' results and monthly passenger statistics in the aftermath of the pandemic, alongside the likes of regulation around sustainable fuels, and the prospects for hydrogen-powered commercial flight. He joins Simple Flying with a lifelong love of all things aviation.

Boeing 777 pilots, like their counterparts on the vast majority of aircraft at most airlines, have set-in-stone parameters they should work within prior to carrying out landings. These ensure what is known as a stable approach and give pilots a clear set of rules to stick to when committing to a landing. If they are not met, the decision should be easy: go around and try again.

But most of the time, flight crews push on with a landing even if the criteria for a stable approach are not met. Thankfully, this does not mean the majority of landings are made in such conditions. However, it leaves a huge disparity between what should be done and what is actually done when it comes to almost all unstable approaches. Why? Well, psychology and the human factor play a huge part in what is really a very short space of time relative to an overall flight.

Whether an approach is stable or not is essentially based on the carriers’ own standard operating procedures (SOPs) being met before a minimum height is reached during descent. That is according to the Flight Safety Foundation (FSF), which coined the term “ stabilized approach ” in its Approach and Landing Accident Reduction (ALAR) toolkit back in 1998. In this, the organization recommended a minimum height of either 1,000 feet (305 meters) or 500 feet (152 meters) above airport elevation in instrument or visual meteorological conditions (IMC or VMC), respectively.

The FSF’s recommendations stretched to specific criteria behind a stable approach. Simply put, these suggested the correct flight path, speed, landing configuration, and rate of descent by 500 feet (152 meters) in good weather, leaving only small control tweaks needed. Some leeway was granted, namely around speed and sink rate. Overall, though, there was a clear-as-day checklist there for airlines and flight crew alike.
FSF stabilized approach criteria in VMC, from Sky Library
The airspeed is not more than the reference landing speed (VREF) plus 20 knots (23 mph / 37 kmh) indicated speed, and not less than VREF
The aircraft is in the correct landing configuration
Sink rate is no greater than 1,000 feet (305 meters) per minute
Power setting is appropriate for the aircraft configuration and is not below the minimum power for the approach as defined by the operating manual
All briefings and checklists have been conducted

All of this aimed to further ensure safety at what is realistically the most dangerous part of a flight. Indeed, the FSF’s toolkit came after its own research found that unstabilized approaches were a causal factor in 66% of 76 accidents and serious incidents during the final stages of those flights between 1984 and 1997. Through the guidance, the organization sought to aid airlines and pilots in preventing aircraft from arriving at runway thresholds too high, too fast, out of alignment, incorrectly configured, or otherwise unprepared for landing .
Almost All Unstable Approaches Result In Landing Anyway

The issue is that the recommendations appeared not to give the industry the overwhelming push the FSF would have desired. Almost two decades after the organization published the toolkit, it cited evidence that showed almost all unstable approaches were still resulting in aircraft touching down in another report.

Some 95% to 97% of flight crews whose aircraft were in an unstable state continued to touch down, its 2017 report into go-around decision-making stated. This problem of go-around policy non-compliance, the FSF went on to conclude, was “ real ” and “ arguably the largest threat to flight safety ” currently. Improving compliance would be “ significant, ” it added.

Among a string of findings that the report laid out, it noted the industry had “ predominantly ” turned to reducing unstable approaches, rather than incorporating go-arounds as standard practice, to avoid accidents in the final stages of flights. But clearly, entirely eradicating unstable approaches was always going to be impossible. When it came to why pilots still pressed on despite finding themselves in such situations, the reasons were plentiful.

It is easy to pass judgment from the outside. Pilots are tasked with safely delivering passengers, and so what seems an overwhelming disregard of parameters put in place to minimize the risk of incidents raises some pretty serious questions. It is important to consider the realities in cockpits, though, in order to paint a picture of why unstable approaches may be ignored. Among the most blatant factors is timing.

Take the 777 from Boeing , which is among the bestselling widebody series ever produced. If traveling long-haul frequently, there is a good chance you will have stepped foot aboard a 777 variant at some point. Pilots behind the controls of a 777 have well under a minute of decision-making time after reaching the vital 500 feet (305 meter) threshold at which an approach should be stable. At an appropriate landing speed of 132 knots (152 mph or 244 km/h), a typical 777 will touch down 35 to 42 seconds after hitting this point.

Boeing itself recommends approach speeds for different 777 variants of between 139 knots (160 mph or 257 km/h) and 150 knots (172 mph or 278 km/h), so this could vary. Either way, the point stands: A pilot might have little over half a minute, while in the thick of bringing an aircraft down safely, to process whether a go-around is required, make that call, and then carry it out. That is not to try and justify landings made following unstable approaches, but the timing factor does offer some useful context.
body_zh: 乔什居住在英国，是一位热心作家，拥有军事史学位。此前，他曾担任财经记者，广泛报道了航空业，报道了疫情后航空公司的业绩和每月乘客统计数据，以及可持续燃料的监管以及氢动力商业航班的前景等。他带着对航空一切事物的终生热爱加入了 Simple Flying。
与大多数航空公司绝大多数飞机上的飞行员一样，波音 777 飞行员在着陆前都有应遵循的固定参数。这些确保了所谓的稳定进近，并为飞行员在着陆时提供了一套明确的规则。如果没有满足，那么决定应该很容易：绕一圈再试一次。
但大多数时候，即使不满足稳定进近的标准，机组人员也会继续着陆。值得庆幸的是，这并不意味着大多数着陆都是在这种条件下进行的。然而，当涉及到几乎所有不稳定的方法时，它在应该做什么和实际做什么之间留下了巨大的差距。为什么？嗯，心理和人为因素在相对于整个飞行而言非常短的时间内发挥着重要作用。
进近是否稳定主要取决于在下降过程中达到最小高度之前是否满足承运商自己的标准操作程序（SOP）。这是根据飞行安全基金会 (FSF) 的说法，该基金会早在 1998 年就在其减少进近和着陆事故 (ALAR) 工具包中创造了“稳定进近”一词。该组织建议在仪表或目视气象条件（IMC 或 VMC）下，最低高度分别为机场海拔以上 1,000 英尺（305 米）或 500 英尺（152 米）。

The FSF’s recommendations stretched to specific criteria behind a stable approach.简而言之，这些建议了正确的飞行路径、速度、着陆配置以及良好天气下 500 英尺（152 米）的下降率，只需要进行小的控制调整。 Some leeway was granted, namely around speed and sink rate. Overall, though, there was a clear-as-day checklist there for airlines and flight crew alike.
VMC 中的 FSF 稳定进近标准，来自天空图书馆
空速不超过参考着陆速度 (VREF) 加 20 节（23 英里/37 公里/小时）指示速度，且不低于 VREF
飞机处于正确的着陆构型
下沉速率不超过每分钟 1,000 英尺（305 米）
功率设置适合飞机配置，并且不低于操作手册定义的进近最小功率
所有简报和清单均已完成
所有这些都是为了进一步确保飞行中实际上最危险的部分的安全。事实上，FSF 的工具包是在其自己的研究发现，在 1984 年至 1997 年间，在这些航班的最后阶段发生的 76 起事故和严重事故中，有 66% 的原因是不稳定的进近。该组织试图通过该指南帮助航空公司和飞行员防止飞机到达跑道入口处过高、过快、不对准、配置错误或没有做好着陆准备。
几乎所有不稳定的进近都会导致着陆
问题在于，这些建议似乎并没有给该行业带来 FSF 所希望的压倒性推动力。该组织发布该工具包近二十年后，在另一份报告中引用了证据，表明几乎所有不稳定的进近仍然导致飞机着陆。
其 2017 年复飞决策报告称，约 95% 至 97% 的飞机处于不稳定状态的机组人员继续着陆。 FSF 继续得出结论，这种不遵守复飞政策的问题是“真实的”，并且“可以说是目前对飞行安全的最大威胁”。它补充说，提高合规性将“意义重大”。
在该报告列出的一系列调查结果中，它指出，该行业“主要”转向减少不稳定进场，而不是将复飞作为标准做法，以避免飞行最后阶段发生事故。但显然，完全消除不稳定的方法始终是不可能的。当谈到为什么飞行员在这种情况下仍然坚持不懈时，原因有很多。
外界很容易做出判断。飞行员的任务是安全运送乘客，因此，似乎对为尽量减少事故风险而制定的参数的极大忽视引发了一些非常严重的问题。然而，重要的是要考虑驾驶舱的现实情况，以便描绘出为什么不稳定的进近可能被忽略的情况。最明显的因素之一是时机。
以波音 777 为例，它是有史以来最畅销的宽体飞机系列之一。如果经常长途旅行，您很有可能在某个时候乘坐过 777 机型。 777 飞机的飞行员在到达关键的 500 英尺（305 米）阈值后，有不到一分钟的决策时间，在该阈值下进近应该是稳定的。在 132 节（152 英里/小时或 244 公里/小时）的适当着陆速度下，典型的 777 飞机将在到达该点后 35 至 42 秒着陆。
波音公司本身建议不同 777 型号的进场速度介于 139 节（160 英里/小时或 257 公里/小时）和 150 节（172 英里/小时或 278 公里/小时）之间，因此这可能会有所不同。无论哪种方式，要点都是成立的：飞行员在紧急将飞机安全降落时可能只有半分钟多一点的时间来处理是否需要复飞，做出决定，然后执行。这并不是为了证明不稳定进场后着陆的合理性，但时间因素确实提供了一些有用的背景。

title_en: Why Flight Attendants Sit Facing Backward During Takeoff & Landing
title_zh: 为什么空乘人员在起飞和降落时面朝后坐
summary: All for good reason, safety first.
summary_zh: 一切都是有充分理由的，安全第一。
body_en: Writer - Patricia joins Simple Flying with over 20 years of experience in aviation. She has served as cabin crew on flights from economy-class through to first-class and on private jets as well as being head of cabin crew and cabin safety focal point. Patricia has a master's level postgraduate diploma in Human Factors in Aviation and has written about aviation since 2010. Based in Dubai/Cyprus.

Have you ever noticed that flight attendants sit facing backward during take-off and landing? While most passenger seats are forward-facing, some business-class configurations have rearward-facing seats, which some passengers dislike; therefore, backward-facing seats are rarely used for passengers.

The jumpseat is a very important part of an aircraft's safety equipment and is designed to protect the crew members during taxiing, takeoff, and landing, which are critical phases of flight when accidents are more likely to occur. It is important that the crew are protected at these times so that they can evacuate the aircraft if necessary.

Flight attendants face backward in their jump seats during takeoff and landing primarily for safety. During a sudden stop or impact, a rear-facing seat backrest absorbs the force across the back, shoulders, and head instead of concentrating it on a strap across the chest, as in a car. The seatback supports the head, neck, and torso during sudden forward deceleration, reducing strain on the spine and neck and improving force distribution.

Rearward-facing seats are safer for the upper torso and reduce the impact on the body in landings or emergencies. Crew seats facing backward are designed to allow brace positions during normal or abnormal takeoff and landing and help protect against debris. That is why infants are encouraged to stay in backward-facing car seats for as long as possible. During sudden deceleration, your body naturally wants to keep moving forward.

The jumpseat protects the crew from severe injury and helps them stay conscious and mobile in an accident, so that they can direct an evacuation and assist passengers in an emergency. They are always positioned near the emergency exits so that they can respond quickly. In the event of an accident, cabin crew are better protected than passengers in forward-facing seats. The crew member needs to be conscious and uninjured in an emergency for a fast, efficient evacuation and to potentially save lives.

Cabin crew jumpseats are almost always facing rearwards. While most face backward toward the tail, some jumpseats face forward or sideways depending on the aircraft type, cabin layout, and door position. They can be single or double jumpseats. Double jumpseats are usually found in the aircraft galleys at the main doors, while single jumpseats are often next to emergency exits throughout the cabin. On private jets, jumpseats are commonly forward- or side-facing depending on type, although they differ from those on commercial jets and may have a different harness and no safety equipment underneath.

Forward- or sideways-facing seats still meet certification rules and use multipoint harnesses and brace positions to protect the crew. The seat base flips up when the crew member stands, so it doesn’t block the exit during an evacuation. The seats are heavily padded around the back and head area and are next to or inside the galley and adjacent to exit doors. A four-point safety harness secures the crew member firmly during take-off and landing. The lap belt must sit low and tight across the pelvis (not the stomach), with shoulder straps snug and free of twists. It has a single release point.

Below each standard crew jumpseat, there is a container that holds the life vest, a torch, and a manual release tool for the oxygen system. An interphone is attached to every seat or double seat for communication with the crew and flight deck . Around the seat and above the seat, there will be a smoke hood, fire gloves, and a fire extinguisher. During the emergency equipment check, crew must ensure the harness is fully functional and fitted correctly.

Facing into the cabin allows crew members to observe the passengers and spot hazards during critical phases of flight. It also ensures passengers follow safety instructions and are seated when the seat belt sign is on. They can typically be used only by airline crew, depending on the airline's policy. There are more jumpseats than the minimum working crew onboard. There are also jumpseats in the flight deck, but there are very strict rules on who can use them.

These seats are strategically located so that the flight attendants have visibility over different areas of the cabin on take-off, landing and whilst taxiing. There is also the potential to spot unruly passengers or if someone is sick and needs help. They also need to prepare for the silent review in case of evacuation and observe outside conditions through the windows to prepare as needed.

However, in the rear or aft galley, this would not be the case as the passengers cannot be seen clearly if the cabin crew are in their harnesses. On some aircraft types, such as the Airbus A320, one cabin crew seat in the aft is stored flat but maneuvered to face forward, and an extra crew member can observe the rear cabin from there if carried.

While rear-facing seats offer strong impact protection, airlines generally keep passenger seats forward-facing due to passenger preference, motion sickness concerns, and structural or weight factors. Aircraft burn more fuel due to heavy rear-facing seats, making them less popular with airlines.

There is also some psychology behind them. Passengers don’t want someone facing opposite them as a rule, as it makes them feel uncomfortable. Some people don't like the sensation of flying backwards, and it could cause motion sickness in some people. It could also be an issue in an evacuation knowing which way to go, as passengers tend to head in the same direction as the door where they entered the aircraft.

Although backward-facing seats are more commonly found in military aircraft, some airlines offer seats that face backward. If you do want to try out a rear-facing airplane seat, opt for business class seats with airlines like American Airlines , United Airlines, Qatar Airways, and British Airways. The brace position for passengers in rearward-facing seats is different from that of the standard brace position.

The cabin crew brace position is specifically designed to prevent the body flailing, protect limbs needed for opening emergency exits, and minimize head and neck injuries during an impact. When facing the back of the aircraft, impact forces push the body backward into the seat. The back and head should be firmly against the seatback and headrest to prevent whiplash. Knees are together, and feet are placed flat forward or back depending on the airline and whether facing forward or rearward.
body_zh: 作家 - Patricia 加入 Simple Flying 时拥有 20 多年的航空经验。她曾在从经济舱到头等舱的航班以及私人飞机上担任机组人员，并担任机组人员负责人和客舱安全协调员。 Patricia 拥有航空人为因素硕士学位研究生文凭，自 2010 年以来一直撰写有关航空的文章。居住在迪拜/塞浦路斯。
您是否注意到空乘人员在起飞和降落时都是面朝后坐的？虽然大多数乘客座椅都是朝前的，但一些商务舱配置有朝后的座椅，一些乘客不喜欢这种情况；因此，乘客很少使用朝后的座位。
折叠座椅是飞机安全设备中非常重要的一部分，旨在在滑行、起飞和着陆过程中保护机组人员，这些阶段是飞行的关键阶段，事故更容易发生。在这些时候保护机组人员非常重要，以便他们可以在必要时撤离飞机。
在起飞和降落时，空乘人员在折叠座椅上面朝后，主要是为了安全。在突然停止或碰撞时，后向座椅靠背会吸收背部、肩膀和头部的力，而不是像汽车那样将力集中在胸部的带子上。座椅靠背在突然向前减速时支撑头部、颈部和躯干，减少脊柱和颈部的压力并改善力的分布。
后向座椅对于上半身来说更安全，可以减少着陆或紧急情况时对身体的影响。面向后方的机组座椅设计用于在正常或异常起飞和着陆期间允许支撑位置，并有助于防止碎片。这就是为什么鼓励婴儿尽可能长时间地坐在朝后的汽车座椅上。在突然减速时，你的身体自然会想要继续前进。
折叠座椅可以保护机组人员免受严重伤害，并帮助他们在事故中保持意识和活动能力，以便他们能够在紧急情况下指挥疏散并协助乘客。他们总是位于紧急出口附近，以便能够快速做出反应。如果发生事故，机组人员比前排座位的乘客受到更好的保护。在紧急情况下，机组人员需要保持清醒且未受伤，以便快速、有效地疏散并可能挽救生命。

Cabin crew jumpseats are almost always facing rearwards.虽然大多数座椅向后朝向机尾，但有些折叠座椅则面向前方或侧向，具体取决于飞机类型、机舱布局和门位置。它们可以是单人或双人跳椅。双人折叠座椅通常位于飞机厨房的主门处，而单人折叠座椅通常位于整个机舱的紧急出口旁边。在私人飞机上，根据类型，折叠座椅通常是向前或侧面的，尽管它们与商用飞机上的不同，并且可能有不同的安全带，并且下方没有安全设备。
前向或侧向座椅仍然符合认证规则，并使用多点安全带和支撑位置来保护机组人员。当机组人员站立时，座椅底座会向上翻转，因此在疏散时不会堵塞出口。座椅的背部和头部区域有厚厚的衬垫，位于厨房旁边或内部，并靠近出口门。四点式安全带在起飞和着陆过程中牢牢保护机组人员。腰带必须低且紧地穿过骨盆（而不是胃），肩带紧贴且无扭曲。它有一个单一的释放点。
每个标准机组人员折叠座椅下方都有一个容器，里面装有救生衣、手电筒和氧气系统手动释放工具。每个座椅或双人座椅上都安装有内部通话器，用于与机组人员和驾驶舱进行通信。座椅周围和座椅上方将配备防烟面罩、防火手套和灭火器。在检查应急设备期间，机组人员必须确保安全带功能完好且安装正确。
面对机舱，机组人员可以观察乘客并在飞行的关键阶段发现危险。它还确保乘客遵守安全说明，并在安全带标志亮起时就座。它们通常只能由航空公司机组人员使用，具体取决于航空公司的政策。折叠座椅的数量超过了船上最低工作人员的数量。飞行甲板上还设有折叠座椅，但对于谁可以使用它们有非常严格的规定。
这些座椅的位置经过精心设计，以便空乘人员在起飞、着陆和滑行时能够看到机舱的不同区域。还有可能发现不守规矩的乘客或有人生病并需要帮助。他们还需要做好疏散时的静默审查准备，并通过窗户观察外界情况，以便根据需要做好准备。
然而，在后部或船尾厨房，情况就不同了，因为如果机组人员系上安全带，乘客就无法被清楚地看到。在某些机型上，例如空客 A320，机尾的一个机组人员座椅可平放，但可以面朝前方，如果携带的话，一名额外的机组人员可以从那里观察后舱。
虽然后向座椅可提供强大的冲击保护，但由于乘客偏好、晕车问题以及结构或重量因素，航空公司通常将乘客座椅朝前设置。由于后向座椅较重，飞机燃烧更多燃油，这使得它们不太受航空公司欢迎。
它们背后也有一定的心理作用。一般来说，乘客不希望有人面对他们，因为这会让他们感到不舒服。有些人不喜欢向后飞行的感觉，这可能会导致一些人晕车。这也可能是疏散时知道该走哪条路的问题，因为乘客往往会朝与进入飞机的门相同的方向前进。
尽管朝后的座椅在军用飞机上更为常见，但一些航空公司也提供朝后的座椅。如果您确实想尝试后向式飞机座椅，请选择美国航空、联合航空、卡塔尔航空和英国航空等航空公司的商务舱座椅。后向座椅乘客的支撑位置与标准支撑位置不同。
机组人员的支撑位置经过专门设计，可防止身体晃动，保护打开紧急出口所需的四肢，并最大限度地减少撞击时头部和颈部的伤害。当面向飞机后部时，冲击力会将身体向后推入座椅。背部和头部应牢固地靠在座椅靠背和头枕上，以防止颈部扭伤。膝盖并拢，双脚向前或向后平放，具体取决于航空公司以及面朝前还是面朝后。

title_en: How Many Lockheed C-5 Galaxies Are Left In 2026?
title_zh: 2026 年还剩下多少个洛克希德 C-5 星系？
summary: The US Air Force has 52 C-5Ms left, and it now plans to fly them until 2050 even as fewer than four in ten are mission capable.
summary_zh: 美国空军还剩下 52 架 C-5M，现在计划将它们飞行到 2050 年，尽管只有不到十分之四的飞机能够执行任务。
body_en: Aaron is an aviation enthusiast and world traveler with a deep interest in aerospace history and technology. He has traveled around the world numerous times, often incorporating visits to aviation museums and historic aircraft collections into his journeys. A native of New Zealand, he is an expert in aviation and maintains a broad interest in a variety of other subjects.

The Lockheed C-5M Super Galaxy is the largest military transport aircraft built for the United States Air Force and the third largest in the world (after the now-destroyed Antonov An-225 and the An-124). A total of 52 Super Galaxies remain active, with the rest in storage, scrapped, written off, or cannibalized for parts. Most flying C-5Ms are upgraded C-5Bs, although there are also some upgraded C-5As.

The US Air Force is the only C-5M operator, and it now plans to keep the type flying far longer than it once expected. Its Fiscal Year 2027 budget request moves the fleet's retirement to FY2050, five years later than the previous plan, even though only about 37% of the jets were mission capable in FY2025. Here is how many C-5s were built, what happened to them, and how many still exist.
The Origin Of The Massive Lockheed C-5 Galaxy

The C-5 Galaxy traces its roots back to 1961, when the US Air Force started looking for a heavy jet-powered aircraft to replace its Douglas C-133 Cargomasters, while also complementing its Lockheed C-141 Starlifters . The US Army also wanted the Air Force to procure a strategic airlifter larger than the Starlifter, able to carry outsized loads. By 1964, the project had led to the 'Heavy Logistics System' program and received proposals from the US's then-existing airplane makers.

The companies in question were Boeing, Douglas, General Dynamics, Lockheed, and Martin Marietta, and their proposals came with engine options provided by General Electric, Curtiss-Wright, and Pratt & Whitney. The Air Force selected the Lockheed design with General Electric's TF39 engines (the first high-bypass turbofan to enter service). The USAF liked the Boeing design but rejected it, and Boeing took elements of it to develop the Boeing 747-100 with Pratt & Whitney engines.

A total of 131 Lockheed C-5 Galaxies were produced, of which 81 were C-5As. In the 1970s, these were found to have cracks in the wings, forcing the Air Force to drastically reduce allowed payloads until new strengthened wings were installed on 77 remaining C-5As between 1981 and 1987.
How Many Lockheed C-5 Galaxies Were Produced?

The Lockheed C-5 Galaxy has been a pivotal air mobility asset for the United States Air Force for decades . It is responsible for the rapid deployment of combat forces to any point in the world at short notice. First delivered in 1970, the Air Force explains that , " the C-5 has seen extensive use in every major global contingency since the Southeast Asia War ."

The massive airlifter provides range and cargo capacity that greatly exceed the capabilities of the airlifters that came before it. Not only do these aircraft transport soldiers, smaller aircraft, helicopters (including three CH-47 Chinooks), armored vehicles, munitions, and supplies, but they can also accommodate two Minuteman Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles. A standard crew is seven: two pilots, two flight engineers, and three loadmasters (see how many crew members it takes to fly a C-5 Galaxy ).
Lockheed C-5M Super Galaxy specifications (per the US Air Force )
4,800 nautical miles with 120,000 pounds of cargo (7,000 nautical miles with no cargo)

One notable operation for the Galaxies came on October 14, 1973. On that day, the C-5s flew the first Operation Nickel Grass mission to resupply Israeli forces during the Yom Kippur War. Operation Nickel Grass saw the United States supply Israel with 22,325 tons of supplies, including tanks, artillery, and ammunition, using C-141 Starlifters and C-5 Galaxies.
Examining The C-5 Galaxy's Different Variants

As stated, Lockheed delivered a total of 81 C-5A variant aircraft, as well as producing the improved C-5B variant. Two C-5As were upgraded to the C-5C standard to carry larger cargo, like satellites. Lockheed proposed the improved re-engined C-5D in the 1990s as an alternative to the McDonnell Douglas C-17 Globemaster III strategic airlifter, and, while this didn't happen, design elements of the C-5D were later used for the C-5M Super Galaxy program.

Lockheed planned to produce a civilian variant of the Galaxy, called the L-500. The company developed a design for both passenger and cargo versions of the aircraft, with the passenger aircraft being able to carry up to 1,000 passengers (far more than an Airbus A380 ). While the designs attracted some interest, in the end, no airlines purchased the aircraft, and it wasn't produced.

In the late 1990s, it was found that 80% of the Galaxy's airframe service life was still remaining, so the USAF embarked on upgrading 52 examples with GE CF6 (General Electric F138-GE-100) engines, the same family of engines that power the Boeing 767 . These produced 22% more thrust, provided a 30% shorter takeoff roll, and other improvements. Other aspects, like avionics, were also upgraded. The Air Force received its first upgraded C-5M in 2008, with work concluding in 2018.

Of the 131 Galaxies produced, Planespotters.net lists six as having been written off. One (66-8303) was damaged beyond repair after a ground fire during maintenance in one of its 12 fuel cells, and another (67-0172) was destroyed by a fire that broke out in the cargo compartment while taxiing. 68-0218 crashed while attempting an emergency landing amid 'Operation Babylift,' where it would have taken Vietnamese orphans to the US as South Vietnam collapsed and the Fall of Saigon neared.

Planespotters.net lists 15 C-5s as scrapped, with another example listed as 'partially scrapped.' These are all older C-5A models built from 1969 to 1972. A further 37 are stored, mostly at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base in Arizona , while one is listed as 'preserved.' That airframe (69-0014) is on display at the Air Mobility Command Museum at Dover Air Force Base. 70-0451 was meant to be displayed at the Travis Air Force Base Heritage Center, but was scrapped after space couldn't be found.

Multiple sources confirm that a total of 52 C-5 Galaxies are listed as active. All of these have been upgraded to the C-5M Super Galaxy standard and are newer airframes, with most of them having been built between 1985 and 1989 and originally delivered as examples of the C-5B Galaxy model. The Air Force now plans to keep them in service until FY2050.
body_zh: 亚伦是一位航空爱好者和环球旅行家，对航空航天历史和技术有着浓厚的兴趣。他曾多次环游世界，经常在旅途中参观航空博物馆和历史飞机收藏。他是新西兰人，是航空专家，并对其他各种学科保持着广泛的兴趣。
洛克希德 C-5M 超级银河是为美国空军制造的最大军用运输机，也是世界第三大军用运输机（仅次于现已被摧毁的安东诺夫 An-225 和 An-124）。总共 52 个超级星系仍然活跃，其余的则被储存、报废、报废或拆解为零件。大多数飞行的 C-5M 都是升级版的 C-5B，但也有一些升级版的 C-5A。
美国空军是唯一的 C-5M 运营商，现在计划让该型飞机的飞行时间远远超过以前的预期。其 2027 财年预算请求将机队的退役时间推迟到 2050 财年，比之前的计划晚了五年，尽管只有约 37% 的飞机能够在 2025 财年执行任务。以下是 C-5 的生产数量、发生的情况以及仍然存在的数量。
巨大的洛克希德 C-5 星系的起源
C-5 Galaxy 的历史可以追溯到 1961 年，当时美国空军开始寻找重型喷气动力飞机来取代其道格拉斯 C-133 Cargomasters，同时也补充其洛克希德 C-141 Starlifters。美国陆军还希望空军采购一架比“星际升降机”更大的战略运输机，能够运载超大型货物。到 1964 年，该项目引发了“重型物流系统”计划，并收到了美国当时的飞机制造商的建议。
这些公司包括波音公司、道格拉斯公司、通用动力公司、洛克希德公司和马丁玛丽埃塔公司，他们的提案中包含通用电气公司、柯蒂斯莱特公司和普惠公司提供的发动机选项。空军选择了洛克希德设计公司的通用电气 TF39 发动机（第一台投入使用的高涵道比涡轮风扇发动机）。美国空军喜欢波音的设计，但拒绝了它，波音吸收了其中的元素，开发了配备普惠发动机的波音 747-100。
洛克希德 C-5 星系总共生产了 131 架，其中 81 架是 C-5A。 20 世纪 70 年代，人们发现这些飞机的机翼存在裂缝，迫使空军大幅减少允许的有效载荷，直到 1981 年至 1987 年间在剩余的 77 架 C-5A 上安装了新的加固机翼。
生产了多少个洛克希德 C-5 星系？
几十年来，洛克希德 C-5 Galaxy 一直是美国空军的关键空中机动资产。它负责在短时间内将作战部队快速部署到世界任何地点。空军于 1970 年首次交付，解释说：“自东南亚战争以来，C-5 在每一次重大全球突发事件中都得到了广泛使用。”
这架大型运输机的航程和货运能力远远超过了之前的运输机。这些飞机不仅可以运输士兵、小型飞机、直升机（包括三架 CH-47 支奴干直升机）、装甲车、弹药和补给品，还可以容纳两枚民兵洲际弹道导弹。标准机组人员为七名：两名飞行员、两名飞行工程师和三名装载管理员（看看驾驶 C-5 Galaxy 需要多少名机组人员）。
洛克希德 C-5M 超级银河规格（根据美国空军）
1973 年 10 月 14 日，银河号执行了一次值得注意的行动。那天，C-5 执行了第一次“镍草行动”任务，在赎罪日战争期间为以色列军队提供补给。在“镍草行动”中，美国使用 C-141 Starlifters 和 C-5 Galaxies 向以色列提供了 22,325 吨物资，包括坦克、大炮和弹药。
检查 C-5 Galaxy 的不同变体
如上所述，洛克希德公司总共交付了 81 架 C-5A 改型飞机，并生产了改进的 C-5B 改型。两架 C-5A 升级为 C-5C 标准，可以运载卫星等更大的货物。洛克希德公司在 20 世纪 90 年代提出改进后的 C-5D 发动机，作为麦道 C-17 环球霸王 III 战略运输机的替代品，虽然这没有实现，但 C-5D 的设计元素后来被用于 C-5M 超级银河计划。
洛克希德计划生产 Galaxy 的民用版本，称为 L-500。该公司开发了客机和货机两种版本的设计，客机最多可搭载 1,000 名乘客（远远超过空客 A380）。虽然这些设计引起了一些兴趣，但最终没有航空公司购买这架飞机，它也没有生产。

20 世纪 90 年代末，发现 Galaxy 的机身使用寿命还剩 80%，因此美国空军开始使用 GE CF6（通用电气 F138-GE-100）发动机对 52 架飞机进行升级，该发动机与波音 767 的发动机属于同一系列。它们产生的推力增加了 22%，起飞滑跑时间缩短了 30%，并进行了其他改进。其他方面，如航空电子设备，也得到了升级。空军于 2008 年接收了第一架升级版 C-5M，工作于 2018 年完成。
在产生的 131 个星系中，Planespotters.net 列出了 6 个已被注销的星系。其中一架 (66-8303) 在维护其 12 个燃料电池之一期间发生地面火灾后损坏无法修复，另一架 (67-0172) 在滑行时因货舱爆发火灾而被摧毁。 68-0218 在“婴儿举升行动”中尝试紧急着陆时坠毁，随着南越的崩溃和西贡陷落的临近，这架飞机将把越南孤儿带到美国。

Planespotters.net 列出了 15 架 C-5 已报废，还有一个例子被列为“部分报废”。这些都是 1969 年至 1972 年生产的较旧的 C-5A 型号。另外 37 架被存放，大部分存放在亚利桑那州的戴维斯-蒙森空军基地，还有一架被列为“保留”。该机身 (69-0014) 陈列在多佛空军基地的空中机动指挥博物馆。 70-0451 原本打算在特拉维斯空军基地遗产中心展示，但因找不到空间而被废弃。
多个消息来源证实，总共有 52 个 C-5 星系被列为活跃星系。所有这些都已升级到 C-5M Super Galaxy 标准，并且是较新的机身，其中大多数是在 1985 年至 1989 年间制造的，最初是作为 C-5B Galaxy 型号的示例交付的。空军现在计划让它们服役到 2050 财年。

title_en: Why A Part 103 Ultralight Needs No Pilot's License In The US & Weighs Under 254 Pounds
title_zh: 为什么 Part 103 超轻型飞机在美国不需要飞行员执照且重量低于 254 磅
summary: A look at single-seat ultralights that trade range and speed for regulatory freedom and strict operating limits.
summary_zh: 看看单座超轻型飞机，以航程和速度换取监管自由和严格的操作限制。
body_en: Ethan is an aviation professional with a degree in Aviation Management with Flight from the Florida Institute of Technology. He previously wrote aviation and tourism features for Florida Tech’s student newspaper, The Crimson , where he developed a clear, reader‑focused reporting style. Aviation journalism has remained a consistent priority throughout his career.

He currently holds a Restricted ATP and Commercial Multi‑Engine Pilot certificate and works in aviation supply chain and aircraft component repair. Alongside his industry role, he is pursuing his Certified Flight Instructor rating and actively building flight experience.
A lifelong aviation enthusiast, Ethan spent countless hours at Raleigh–Durham International Airport’s observation deck studying air traffic and practicing amateur photography and videography.

Many people assume that flying any type of aircraft requires extensive training, a pilot certificate, medical approval, and federal registration. While that holds true for most types of licenses, such as a Certified Flight Instructor certificate (CFI) or Airline Transport Pilot (ATP), the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has long maintained a narrow exception that allows certain recreational flyers to take to the skies without obtaining a pilot license. The exception falls under FAA Part 103 , a section of federal regulations governing ultralight vehicles and the strict limitations placed upon them.

While Part 103 is broadly described as allowing someone to fly without a license, the reality is more nuanced. The regulation applies only to a highly specific category of lightweight recreational aircraft that must meet strict performance, weight, and operating requirements. Understanding what qualifies under Part 103 helps explain where the FAA draws the line between recreational freedom and traditional pilot certification requirements.

Yes, you can legally fly an aircraft in the United States without a pilot certificate, but only if the aircraft qualifies as an ultralight vehicle under FAA Part 103. These vehicles occupy a unique regulatory category that exempts operators from requirements including pilot licensing, aircraft registration, airworthiness certification, and medical certification. The exemption was created to support recreational flying while limiting risk through strict aircraft performance restrictions.

For powered ultralights, the FAA limits empty weight to 254 lb (115.2 kg), fuel capacity to five gallons (18.9 liters), maximum level-flight speed to 55 knots, and maximum power-off stall speed to 24 knots. Because these aircraft are intentionally small and limited in capability, the FAA regulates them differently than conventional airplanes.

The concept dates back decades, when regulators sought a framework that would allow simple recreational flying without imposing the full regulatory burden associated with general aviation aircraft. Rather than focusing on pilot certification, Part 103 controls risk by limiting what the aircraft can do. According to the FAA's regulations, qualifying ultralight vehicles are intended solely for sport and recreational purposes and are limited to carrying a single occupant.
What Requirements Must An Aircraft Meet Under Part 103?

A common misconception is that any small aircraft can be flown without a license. In reality, FAA Part 103 sets detailed technical requirements an aircraft must meet to qualify as an ultralight vehicle. The term Ultralight is a specific category issued by the FAA for licensing and certification, such as airplane, rotorcraft, or glider for pilot ratings. While an FAA certificate typically prints the category and class, the lack of a true license requirement omits this display.

The most important requirements involve weight, occupancy, fuel capacity, and performance. Powered Ultralights operate on the basis of minimal configurations of these variables. Ultralight aircraft should not be confused with Light Sport Aircraft, the next category up in the FAA's classification; they also have slightly different regulatory requirements, such as a higher speed limit of 250 knots and the ability to carry an additional passenger. These privileges come at the cost of training for a sport pilot certificate, among other requirements as outlined in 14 CFR Part 61, Subpart J, and 14 CFR Part 91.327.

Unpowered ultralights, such as many hang gliders, fall under a different weight limit. Under Part 103, these vehicles must weigh less than 155 pounds (70.3 kg) empty. By restricting both weight and performance, the FAA effectively prevents Part 103 aircraft from evolving into conventional airplanes that would normally require certification and pilot qualification.

Although operators are exempt from licensing requirements, they are not exempt from federal aviation regulations. FAA Part 103 establishes operational limitations designed to protect both ultralight pilots and the public on the ground. Interestingly enough, Ultralight aircraft are not governed by either 14 CFR Part 61 or Part 91, which is the usual home for general aviation operation guidelines.

Among the most important restrictions are where and when ultralights may fly. Operations are generally limited to daylight hours and must avoid congested areas, cities, towns, and open-air assemblies of people. The rules also restrict operations within controlled airspace (Class A, B, C, D, E, and most special use airspace) unless prior authorization has been obtained from air traffic control .

These requirements show that the FAA's approach is not deregulation but targeted regulation. Operators may not need a pilot certificate, but they are still responsible for understanding airspace, weather conditions, and applicable operating restrictions before every flight. For many ultralight enthusiasts, voluntary training remains a common safety practice despite the absence of a licensing requirement.
What Do Aviation Organizations And Experts Recommend?

While FAA regulations do not require formal flight training for Part 103 operations, aviation organizations consistently encourage it. Groups such as the Experimental Aircraft Association (EAA) have long promoted structured training programs for ultralight pilots, emphasizing that regulatory exemptions do not eliminate the risks associated with flight.
body_zh: Ethan 是一名航空专业人士，拥有佛罗里达理工学院飞行管理学位。他此前曾为佛罗里达理工学院的学生报纸《The Crimson》撰写航空和旅游专题文章，在那里他开发了一种清晰、以读者为中心的报道风格。在他的整个职业生涯中，航空新闻始终是优先考虑的事情。
他目前持有受限 ATP 和商业多引擎飞行员证书，从事航空供应链和飞机部件维修工作。除了他的行业角色外，他还追求认证飞行教练评级并积极积累飞行经验。
伊森是一位终生的航空爱好者，他在罗利-达勒姆国际机场的观景台上花费了无数时间研究空中交通并练习业余摄影和摄像。
许多人认为驾驶任何类型的飞机都需要大量的培训、飞行员证书、医疗许可和联邦注册。虽然大多数类型的执照都是如此，例如认证飞行教官证书（CFI）或航空公司运输飞行员证书（ATP），但美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）长期以来一直保留着一个狭隘的例外，允许某些休闲飞行者在没有获得飞行员执照的情况下飞上天空。该例外属于 FAA 第 103 部分的规定，该部分是管理超轻型车辆及其严格限制的联邦法规的一部分。
虽然第 103 部分被广泛描述为允许某人在没有许可证的情况下飞行，但现实情况更加微妙。该法规仅适用于必须满足严格的性能、重量和操作要求的高度特定类别的轻型休闲飞机。了解第 103 部分规定的资格有助于解释 FAA 在娱乐自由和传统飞行员认证要求之间划定的界限。
是的，您可以在没有飞行员证书的情况下在美国合法驾驶飞机，但前提是飞机符合 FAA 第 103 部分规定的超轻型车辆。这些车辆属于独特的监管类别，可免除运营商的要求，包括飞行员执照、飞机注册、适航认证和医疗认证。这项豁免的目的是支持休闲飞行，同时通过严格的飞机性能限制来限制风险。
对于动力超轻型飞机，FAA 将空重限制为 254 磅（115.2 千克），燃油容量限制为 5 加仑（18.9 升），最大平飞速度限制为 55 节，最大断电失速速度限制为 24 节。由于这些飞机故意设计得较小且性能有限，因此美国联邦航空局对它们的监管与传统飞机不同。
这个概念可以追溯到几十年前，当时监管机构正在寻求一个框架，允许简单的休闲飞行，而不需要承担与通用航空飞机相关的全部监管负担。第 103 部分不是专注于飞行员认证，而是通过限制飞机的功能来控制风险。根据美国联邦航空局的规定，合格的超轻型车辆仅用于运动和娱乐目的，并且仅限于搭载一名乘员。
飞机必须满足第 103 部分的哪些要求？
一个常见的误解是任何小型飞机都可以在没有许可证的情况下飞行。事实上，FAA 第 103 部分规定了飞机必须满足超轻型车辆资格的详细技术要求。术语“超轻型”是美国联邦航空局颁发的用于许可和认证的特定类别，例如飞机、旋翼机或滑翔机的飞行员等级。虽然 FAA 证书通常会打印类别和等级，但缺乏真正的许可证要求会忽略此显示。

最重要的要求包括重量、占用率、燃料容量和性能。动力超轻型飞机在这些变量的最小配置的基础上运行。超轻型飞机不应与轻型运动飞机混淆，轻型运动飞机是美国联邦航空局分类中的下一个类别；它们的监管要求也略有不同，例如 250 节的更高速度限制以及承载额外乘客的能力。这些特权的代价是获得运动飞行员证书的培训费用，以及 14 CFR 第 61 部分、J 部分和 14 CFR 第 91.327 部分中概述的其他要求。
无动力超轻型飞机，例如许多悬挂式滑翔机，有不同的重量限制。根据第 103 部分，这些车辆的空重必须低于 155 磅（70.3 公斤）。通过限制重量和性能，FAA 有效地防止了第 103 部分飞机演变为通常需要认证和飞行员资格的传统飞机。
尽管运营商不受许可要求的约束，但他们并不能免除联邦航空法规的约束。 FAA 第 103 部分规定了旨在保护超轻型飞行员和地面公众的操作限制。有趣的是，超轻型飞机不受 14 CFR 第 61 部分或第 91 部分管辖，而后者通常是通用航空运营指南的所在地。
其中最重要的限制是超轻型飞机可以飞行的地点和时间。行动通常仅限于白天，并且必须避开拥挤的地区、城市、城镇和露天人群集会。这些规则还限制在受控空域（A、B、C、D、E 类和大多数特殊用途空域）内进行操作，除非事先获得空中交通管制部门的授权。
这些要求表明，FAA的做法不是放松管制，而是有针对性的监管。运营商可能不需要飞行员证书，但他们仍然有责任在每次飞行前了解空域、天气状况和适用的操作限制。对于许多超轻爱好者来说，尽管没有执照要求，但自愿培训仍然是一种常见的安全做法。
航空组织和专家有何建议？
虽然 FAA 法规并不要求针对第 103 部分操作进行正式的飞行培训，但航空组织始终鼓励这样做。实验飞机协会（EAA）等团体长期以来一直在推动超轻型飞行员的结构化培训计划，强调监管豁免并不能消除与飞行相关的风险。

title_en: How JetBlue's Bag Fee Hike Makes A BlueFirst Base Fare From $249, Bag Included, Look Like A Real Alternative
title_zh: 捷蓝航空 (JetBlue) 行李费上调如何让 BlueFirst 基本票价从 249 美元起（含行李）看起来像是一个真正的选择
summary: Why JetBlue's new first class is actually quite compelling on price, and why this could be a problem.
summary_zh: 为什么捷蓝航空的新头等舱在价格上实际上相当有吸引力，以及为什么这可能是一个问题。
body_en: Daniel comes to Simple Flying with a business focused approach to the aviation world. Daniel enjoys analyzing strategy and how companies move against each other to gain a step ahead in the skies. Besides strategy, Daniel also has a passion for aircraft design and the history of aviation.

Changes are happening at JetBlue Airways . The airline recently raised its bag fees for economy passengers; as of November 3, the first checked bag will cost between $50 and $70, depending on the day and when the ticket is booked, while a second checked bag ranges from $70 to $85. These are steep prices and noticeably higher than the checked bag fees set by US legacy carriers, while JetBlue's base fares before optional add-ons tend to be lower than the competition.

At the same time, JetBlue will soon introduce 'BlueFirst', a domestic first class cabin that will be rolled out fleetwide. The carrier will debut this cabin on December 8 on its route from Boston to Fort Lauderdale, before introducing the cabin throughout its network. While JetBlue prices all fares dynamically, BlueFirst one-way fares will start at $249 when the cabin is first introduced, and while this certainly doesn't mean all tickets will be priced this way, those that are will be very compelling compared with the airline's economy cabin.

JetBlue offers three fare types for its Main, EvenMore, BlueFirst, and Mint cabin classes: Base, Standard, and Flex. None of the fares for Main and EvenMore include checked bags, meaning passengers who want to check their bags need to add at least $50 to the overall price of their tickets. At the same time, the airline's new BlueFirst fares do include at least one checked bag, while the BlueFirst Flex fare includes two checked bags. What makes this particularly notable is that BlueFirst fares are actually fairly attractive.

The airline's one-way BlueFirst fares start at $299 from Boston to Fort Lauderdale, and the route between LaGuardia and Fort Lauderdale follows shortly afterward, with prices starting at $249. Although most tickets are being sold for significantly more, the airline has largely priced BlueFirst fares at about 40% to 70% more than an equivalent Main ticket.

Crucially, however, even the BlueFirst Base ticket includes a checked bag, slightly closing the gap. The BlueFirst Flex includes two checked bags, whereas a Main Flex or an EvenMore Flex fare includes none. While the full cost of a BlueFirst ticket will still be higher, it's closer than expected.

With the recent increase in bag fees, BlueFirst tickets do look quite attractive for passengers who will check a bag and are willing to pay more for a better experience . BlueFirst offers a large recliner with added legroom, as well as complimentary meals and premium drinks. It undoubtedly offers a more comfortable experience than Main, and the price difference is not particularly steep once ancillaries are factored. What's more, JetBlue's initial pricing for BlueFirst does not follow the standard practice in the US.

Generally, the US legacy carriers (which are the airlines that have offered domestic first class the longest) do not price first class tickets at 40% to 70% above economy. Domestic first class fares are usually significantly more expensive than economy tickets, and even when you factor in ancillaries, first class comes at a real price premium. Admittedly, JetBlue's initial BlueFirst tickets are being sold in the competitive Florida market, where fares tend to be low, but they still largely undercut the legacy carriers on price.

One way to view this is as a deliberate strategy by JetBlue. The airline has never before offered a domestic first class cabin, and it plans to introduce BlueFirst throughout the network fairly rapidly. Not only do potential customers need to be made aware of the product and exposed to it, but the carrier also needs to pull customers away from American , Delta , and United . Attractive initial fares help with publicity while increasing bookings, which heightens awareness.

On the flip side, however, airlines generally charge what they think is the maximum price that customers are willing to pay. JetBlue undercutting competitors on price can also be seen as a reflection of the carrier's pricing power, which isn't a positive sign. One reason JetBlue introduced BlueFirst was to increase revenue, since first class generally commands higher fares. If it continues to undercut competitors on price system-wide, then this would become a problem.

JetBlue operates like a budget airline, such as Frontier or Allegiant Air. However, the airline has differentiated itself not necessarily through low fares, but through the passenger experience. The carrier offered significantly more legroom in economy, along with seatback screens before they became common on domestic flights. In addition, snack options were diverse, and the airline's later Mint business class on transcontinental and transatlantic routes has been well received.

Despite its low-cost carrier structure, the airline offers a passenger experience similar to that of legacy carriers, and arguably better in some ways. However, JetBlue has been unable to command a fare premium for its excellent economy product, while its Northeast operations come with high operating costs. In addition, the airline didn't offer first class in the past, further limiting revenue, and the carrier has faced serious challenges expanding its customer base.
